condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is moclobemide; L3 human records show rapid oral absorption with Tmax about 1.44–1.46 h after single oral dosing.

Close structural analog procainamide and its metabolite NAPA have measured absolute oral bioavailability values of 68–92%, with L2 context of 75–85% and acecainide 85%, all well above the 20% threshold.

L4 records show high fraction absorbed for related or similarly small oral drugs (NAPA 87–92%, cetirizine/levocetirizine ≥85%, bepotastine >85%, isoniazid Fa 0.97–0.99, rivaroxaban 80–100%), supporting favorable intestinal absorption.

L5 bidirectional permeability records show high permeability and low efflux for diverse compounds, including morpholine-amide-containing molecules, rivaroxaban, fexofenadine, MMB, and compound 5v; no supplied record indicates significant gut-wall efflux or intestinal metabolism for the query or close analogs. Duplicate cards of the same measurements are not counted independently.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for moclobemide itself was supplied; the decision relies on structural analogy to procainamide/NAPA, the physicochemical prior, and indirect exposure/absorption/efflux records.
No fed-state-specific moclobemide bioavailability or absorption record is available; the fed condition is not shown to reduce F below 20%.
L5 records are for other molecules rather than moclobemide, so their transfer is inferential rather than direct.
No direct intestinal metabolism or first-pass clearance quantification for moclobemide was supplied.
L5 contains no intestinal metabolism records, only permeability/efflux evidence.
